title: Four years with Marable, Oklahoma City, and leaving for New York
summary: Marable drilled him daily and marked his music. He left for a year in Oklahoma City, returned, then left for New York on Red Allen's wire with Marable's blessing.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Because he really, he really did. He helped me. He drilled me from, from the time, from seven o'clock in the morning up until noon, it's time to eat. Then, then the big band rehearsals, see. But, what he used to do, he marked, marked my music, and where, marked the fingering on my instrument. Then I knew a little bass horn, I could play it on either instrument then, see. I got so, coming up, the bass horn, and, and the bass string bass. Because I, I knew, I, I, there's one good thing about it. I started learning the instrument. To know the, the, the finger of the instrument, see. Then, and he just put the fingering under the music. He said, now these same notes, it's just like that. I said, you're supposed to play. And we started, he played the bass on the piano and everything, and like that, and, and up I went. And I stayed with him four years. Four years. And he says, when you, when I turn you loose, you can go. He said, but don't leave until I tell you, you can go. He said, they all leave me. That's what he, he always said. He says, everyone I've had, sooner or later they, they'll leave. And that's what's true. So, so finally I, I, I start getting wires from, uh, Red Allen, New York. You see, I was in St. Louis, you see. So, so, so I went, first year, that last year, I said, I said, well, maybe I might, I might go to New York. So, finally, I was with me, just before, I left, I left the boat, I left the boat, uh, I went to Oklahoma City. Yeah, I left the boat one year. And I went to Oklahoma City with Alvin Fats Wall. I didn't go down New Orleans, you see. And the following summer, we went back on the boat, see. Uh, a boy by the name of Eugene Hill, Slim they call him. He's out in Minnesota now. That's, he's around Chicago now. I, I saw him not very long ago. What did he play? A drummer. He was a drummer, yes. And, uh, God gifted music world. That's what you see, you know, I am Eugene Hill, God gifted music world. So, so, so, so him and I, we went out in Oklahoma City, a fellow by the name of Alvin Fats Wall, a fine musician. And that's where I ran into another fast, fast group. All fine musicians. Young and new. They, they can read. But I was ready, though. I was ready for them. And I think that helped me a hundred percent, because when I left there and come back on the boat, I was really walking. And I would sit right in there with feet and him. And he was just laughing. He says, oh yeah, you're getting slick now, eh. You know, that's what he used to tell me. Well, I said, so, I made one, one season with them in St. Louis. And so, I, I, I told him, I says, I says, I think, I said, I got a wire from Ray Allen. I said, I think I'm going, I'm going to New York. He says, well, well, Al, he says, I must tell you. He said, well, you ready? He said, you just go ahead on. If you want to go, it's okay. I won't stop you, but I want you to go when you was right. I said, you ready? You tell him I sent you. Just like that. That's the way he used to talk. You tell him I sent you. So, when I left there, I had my bass horn and bass fiddle, and I could play both of them. And as years rolled by, I got to New York, and start getting around with fast company, and everybody, I must be ready, because everybody was somebody I'd sit in and played with, with the best around New York.
